html:
A rising of the Pueblo peoples of New Mexico against Spanish rule in August 1680, the most successful Indigenous revolt against Spain in North America. It drove the Spanish out of New Mexico for twelve years.

Spanish rule had brought forced labour and tribute, and friars who banned the old religion, raided kivas and punished ceremonial leaders. Drought, famine and Apache raids made life worse. In 1675 the governor had dozens of religious leaders arrested and whipped. One of them, Popé of Ohkay Owingeh, organised a secret plan among towns speaking several languages, using knotted cords to count down the days.

On 10 August the Pueblos rose together. They killed about 400 Spaniards, including 21 friars, besieged Santa Fe and forced the survivors to retreat south along the Camino Real to El Paso. Churches were destroyed. The Spanish returned under Diego de Vargas in 1692. Afterward Spanish rule was milder, and the Pueblos kept their languages and ceremonies, which survive today.
sum: A rising of the Pueblo peoples of New Mexico against Spanish rule in August 1680, the most successful Indigenous revolt against Spain in North America. It drove the Spanish out of New Mexico for twelve years.
